DRDO has given quantum jump to India's pursuit of self-reliance in defence: Chairman Samir V Kamat. Addressing a gathering at an event, DRDO Chairman Samir V Kamat said the efforts of DRDO have given a "quantum jump" to India's pursuit of self-reliance in defence as part of the 'Aatmanirbhar Bharat' vision. Kamat stressed that DRDO should focus on working together with all stakeholders in the defence ecosphere to meet the country's futuristic challenges and fulfill Prime Minister Narendra Modi's vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat. Kamat called upon DRDO scientists to focus on next-generation needs, including cyber security, space, and artificial intelligence. fusion_ranked_evidence.title: India conducts maiden flight test of ‘Kusha' long-range SAM - Janes
fusion_ranked_evidence.snippet: # India conducts maiden flight test of ‘Kusha' long-range SAM. The ‘Kusha' long-range surface-to-air missile launches from a vertical-launch system during its maiden flight test. India's state-owned Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) has conducted the maiden flight test of its ‘Kusha' long-range surface-to-air missile (SAM). The Indian Ministry of Defence (MoD) said on 23 July that the test was conducted against an electronic target simulating a “high-speed and high-altitude aerial threat” at Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island off the northeastern coast of Odisha. The MoD added that the electronic target was “successfully intercepted by the missile system”. *Janes* analysis of imagery released by the MoD indicates that the missile features a cylindrical fuselage topped by a pointed nose cone, possibly indicating the presence of a radome housing a guidance seeker. Small forward control surfaces are positioned immediately aft of the nose section, while a second set of smaller fins is located around the missile's mid-body.

fusion_ranked_evidence.title: India develops expendable turbojet engine - Janes
fusion_ranked_evidence.snippet: # India develops expendable turbojet engine. India's expendable turbojet engine in the 350 kg-thrust class. India's state-owned Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) has developed a 350 kg-thrust expendable turbojet engine, the Ministry of Defence (MoD) announced on 23 July. The engine – developed by the DRDO's Gas Turbine Research Establishment (GTRE) – is being manufactured by Hyderabad-based Azad Engineering, the MoD said. The first unit was manufactured and delivered to GTRE on 22 July. The system is India's first domestically developed expendable turbojet engine and forms part of broader efforts to reduce dependence on imported propulsion technologies. An expendable turbojet engine is a single-use gas turbine designed to operate for a short-duration mission. fusion_ranked_evidence.snippet: Addressing a gathering at an event, DRDO Chairman Samir V Kamat said the efforts of DRDO have given a “quantum jump” to India’s pursuit of self-reliance in defence as part of the ‘Aatmanirbhar Bharat’ vision. He expressed satisfaction that 22 Acceptance of Necessity (AoN) been accorded by the Defence Acquisition Council (DAC) and the Services Procurement Board (SPB) for the induction of several DRDO-developed systems worth approximately Rs 1.30 lakh crore to be manufactured by Indian industries in 2025, which is the “highest in any single year in history”, according to the statement. Kamat also said that 11 contracts for acquisitions valued at Rs 26,000 crore have been signed with DRDO production partners for Nag missile system, Ashwini low-level transportable radar, air defence fire control radar (ADFCR), electronic warfare suite for Mi-17 V5 helicopter, area denial munition (ADM) Type-1 and high explosive pre-fragmented (HEPF) Mk-I (enhanced) for the Pinaka multiple launch rocket system, among other systems.

fusion_ranked_evidence.title: From Concept to Cockpit: DRDO Demonstrates First Ever Morphing Wing in Flight a Major Breakthrough in Indian Aerospace Self - Reliance - Indian Masterminds
fusion_ranked_evidence.snippet: # From Concept to Cockpit: DRDO Demonstrates First Ever Morphing Wing in Flight a Major Breakthrough in Indian Aerospace Self – Reliance. India’s DRDO has successfully tested a wing that can change shape mid-flight — a breakthrough that could revolutionize future Indian fighters and UAVs with added stealth, agility, and efficiency. New Delhi: India took a major stride in aerospace innovation: the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) has successfully tested a “*morphing wing*” — a fighter-jet wing whose shape can change dynamically in flight. According to DRDO and related defence-analysis reports, the objective is to integrate morphing wings — along with other advanced technologies like nano-stealth coatings and fiber-optic (fly-by-light) avionics — into India’s sixth-generation fighter programs. With the world’s major powers racing towards 6th-generation fighters (with technologies like adaptive wings, AI/autonomy, directed-energy weapons, sensor fusion), India’s morphing-wing breakthrough could anchor its long-term air-power roadmap — influencing projects well beyond the next decade.

fusion_ranked_evidence.title: India progresses AEW&C Mk 2 programme with new contracts - Janes
fusion_ranked_evidence.snippet: CABS' Mk II AEW&C programme is based on A321 platform. India's Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) has awarded two contracts in support of its indigenous Netra Mk II airborne early warning & control (AEW&C) special mission aircraft programme. The Mk II is based on the Airbus A321, with DRDO's Centre for AirBorne Systems (CABS) aiming to provide the Indian Air Force (IAF) with six platforms. On 22 July, CABS signed a contract with Air India Engineering Services Limited (AIESL) to convert six A321 airframes acquired from Air India from their current “commercial configuration to [a] green configuration”, the Ministry of Defence (MoD) said. In a separate contract that same day, CABS also contracted Adani Defence Systems and Technologies (ADSTL) as the programme's Development cum Production Partner (DcPP), the MoD said. ADSTL will design mission systems for the Netra Mk II platforms, the MoD added. CABS and ADSTL will begin the process of integrating mission systems on the platforms after their delivery by Airbus, the MoD said.

fusion_ranked_evidence.snippet: **New Delhi:** India has achieved a significant breakthrough in the field of aerospace and defence technology with the successful development of the country’s **first indigenous Expendable Turbo Jet Engine in the 350 kg thrust class**. The successful delivery of this sophisticated engine, based on **DRDO’s indigenous design**, highlights the growing technological capabilities of India’s defence industry and strengthens the country’s journey towards self-reliance in critical defence technologies. **Defence Secretary, Secretary of Department of Defence R&D and Chairman, DRDO Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh** congratulated the GTRE–industry partnership, stating that the collaboration has played a crucial role in converting a technological vision into a historic milestone for India’s defence manufacturing sector. The achievement is expected to further strengthen India’s indigenous aerospace capabilities and support the development of advanced defence systems in the future.

fusion_ranked_evidence.title: DRDO completes trials of drone launched unmanned precision guided missile; Defence Minister terms it a strategic milestone | Akashvani News - News On AIR
fusion_ranked_evidence.snippet: ## DRDO completes trials of drone launched unmanned precision guided missile; Defence Minister terms it a strategic milestone. The Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) has successfully completed the final development trials of the Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Launched Precision Guided Missile (ULPGM)-V3, marking a significant achievement for the country’s defence sector. The trials were conducted in both air-to-ground and air-to-air modes at the DRDO test range near Kurnool. Developed entirely within the country, the project highlights the growing strength of India’s domestic defence manufacturing ecosystem with the participation of MSMEs and private industries under the Aatmanirbhar Bharat initiative. The missile system was integrated on UAVs developed by NewSpace Research and Technologies for the trials. The successful completion of the tests has cleared the way for serial production of the missile system, further strengthening India’s indigenous defence capabilities. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh has complimented the DRDO, public sector undertakings, defence production partners and industry for the successful development trials of ULPGM-V3.
